//: One shell per case the per-feature provider-agreement check has to get right (spec 171 FR-035-FR-039). Every shell here is authored the way a real host authors one: CShells:Shells:<name>:Features:<feature>:<setting>.

unset-offender.Name: unset-offender
unset-offender.//: User Story 1 scenario 5: one feature set to PostgreSql, another left at its own Sqlite default.

dashboard-only.Name: dashboard-only
dashboard-only.//: The one mapped feature with no Provider setting at all. It is skipped, not defaulted to Sqlite.

disabled-offender.Name: disabled-offender
disabled-offender.//: A feature that would disagree, turned off. A feature a shell does not enable is ignored.

overlay.Name: overlay
overlay.//: Sqlite here, PostgreSql in shells.Production.json. Which one the check sees proves which files it read.

secrets.Name: secrets
secrets.//: Carries a connection string, as a real shell does. Nothing but Provider may ever leave this file.

array-shape.Name: array-shape
array-shape.//: CShells also accepts an array of feature entries. A host that authored this shape must not read as 'nothing enabled'.
